content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks with no errors in `out/`, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 388 bytes (min+gzip), with 87 bytes of own code.

I couldn't run the original against the new file. `lodash` isn't installed in the project, so `src/module.ts` has no resolvable imports. I did not install it, as you asked. `tsc` still reports the three `lodash/...` imports in `src/module.ts` as unresolved. I have no size or output baseline from the original, so check (4) is unconfirmed.

I read the declarations in the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2 and chose these replacements:

- **`tokens`:** I used `words` from the root `es-toolkit`. It matched the lodash-compatible `words` in `es-toolkit/compat` on your two examples and some extra edge cases. It also matched on 200,000 random strings from the allowed character set (ASCII letters, digits, space, hyphen, underscore, period). I could not compare against lodash itself.
- **`byAge`:** I used the root `groupBy` with a small adapter, `(r) => r.age`. The root version needs a function rather than the `'age'` string shorthand. The compat `groupBy` kept the string shorthand but came to 3200 bytes, against 388 for the root version. Both give string keys, so the result shape is the same.
- **`toLookup`:** `fromPairs` exists only in `es-toolkit/compat`, so I imported it from there. It is the only compat import left, and no lodash import remains.
